# Orientation-resolved facet flux for common minimizing caps

This note strengthens the necessary equality-cap inequality in
`candidate f2d1fbdd5a877f5b`. It does not
imply exclusion of a global depth plateau for arbitrary faceted fibers;
the later exact counterexample cited in Section 5 disproves that
exclusion in every continuous dimension.

## 1. The exact one-cap inequality

Let d>=1, and let mu be the sum of d-volume on finitely many positive
full-dimensional compact convex fibers. Suppose a nonvertical cap
H={L>=0} minimizes mass among containing caps at each of two distinct
points y_0,y_1 in the interiors of their respective fibers, and
L(y_0)=L(y_1)=0. Their bases may coincide. Normalize the continuous
normal of L to Euclidean norm one. Let h be ANY ambient affine
functional satisfying h(y_0)=0 and h(y_1)=1.

Let sigma denote the sum of full (d-1)-dimensional section measure
on the fiber sections {L=0}; for d=1 use H_0. Divide these sections
into three disjoint labeled classes:

* P: proper sections, whose plane meets the fiber interior;
* E: supporting sections with the entire fiber in {L<=0};
* F: supporting sections with the entire fiber in {L>=0}.

Positive-volume fibers cannot belong to both E and F. Sections of
zero (d-1)-measure cause no ambiguity. Put

  A=sigma(P)>0,    m=int_P h d sigma,
  delta(w)=dist(h(w),[0,1]).

Then

  A + int_F (1+delta) d sigma <= int_E delta d sigma.       (1)

In particular only EMPTY-side supporting faces outside the endpoint
slab can pay the positive proper-section cost. FULL-side supporting
faces add a penalty, even when they lie inside the slab.

Proof. Pivot at endpoint e with L+t(h-h(y_e)). This margin remains
nonvertical near t=0 and its cap contains y_e for both signs of t.
Write D_e^- and D_e^+ for its left and right mass derivatives at 0.
Local minimality implies D_e^-<=0<=D_e^+.

The exact derivatives needed here are

  D_0^- = m + int_E min(h,0) d sigma + int_F h_+ d sigma,
  D_1^+ = m-A + int_E (h-1)_+ d sigma
                    + int_F min(h-1,0) d sigma.            (2)

For clarity, these are genuine one-sided derivatives, not an
independently chosen collection of Clarke trace weights. At a fixed
fiber use orthonormal continuous coordinates (xi,s) with L=s and
h=h_0(xi)+b s. The perturbed cap is

  s >= -t(h_0-h(y_e))/(1+t b).

At proper sections both derivatives equal int(h_0-h(y_e)). At an E
face only positive inward threshold displacements add mass, giving
right derivative int(h_0-h(y_e))_+ and left derivative
int min(h_0-h(y_e),0). At an F face these formulas are interchanged.
On the relative interior of a positive-area supporting face the
one-sided slice indicators converge to that of the face; convex
interpolation with an interior point and compactness establish this
convergence. Its relative boundary has measure zero. At a zero-area
face the slab mass is o(|t|). The same argument applies at proper
sections. Uniform boundedness of h and all fibers supplies the
dominated-convergence bound. For d=1 the formulas are exactly the
two derivatives of an interval's clipped length.

Since D_1^+-D_0^->=0, subtraction in (2) gives

  A <= int_E [(h-1)_+-min(h,0)] d sigma
       + int_F [min(h-1,0)-h_+] d sigma.

For EVERY real h the two brackets are respectively delta and
-1-delta. This proves (1), including boundary values h=0,1. QED.

If h depends only on the integer base, (1) is the finite sum

  A + sum_(z in F) B_z[1+dist(h(z),[0,1])]
      <= sum_(z in E) B_z dist(h(z),[0,1]),                (3)

where B_z is the supporting section measure. No fiber is discarded
for lying on a cap boundary.

## 2. Simultaneous balanced critical circuits

Suppose y_0,y_1 and an intermediate mixed-integer point are GLOBAL
maximizers of positive depth beta. The finite-tilt attainment,
strict own-fiber slab argument, and finite closed critical-cap cover
proved in the cited note give actual common minimizing caps
H_1,...,H_s and positive coefficients lambda_i such that

  s<=d+1,   sum_i lambda_i=1,   sum_i lambda_i u_i=0.

Every cap has mass beta mu(S), contains both endpoints on its
boundary, and its continuous normal has norm one. For the SAME h,
let A_i,E_i,F_i,sigma_i be its section data. Multiplying (1) by
lambda_i and summing yields the rigorous aggregate constraint

  sum_i lambda_i A_i
    + sum_i lambda_i int_(F_i)(1+delta) d sigma_i
       <= sum_i lambda_i int_(E_i) delta d sigma_i.        (4)

Every A_i is positive. Normal balance does not by itself cancel the
right side: the section measures, integer bases, and supporting
faces depend on i. Formula (4) explicitly retains all those data.
In particular, ANY proposed balanced critical circuit lacking an
empty-side supporting face outside the common slab is impossible.
This is a necessary incidence-and-measure condition, not an OC
allocation inequality.

## 3. An exact orientation test on the layered-cube example

In the actual interval family

  ||z||_infinity<=2,    ||z||_infinity-2 <= x <= T,  T>0,

take endpoints (-e_1,0),(e_1,0), h(z)=(z_1+1)/2. For H={x<=0}
there are 3^n proper sections and all supporting sections are E.
The exterior supporting contribution is 5^(n-1), so (1) reduces to

  3^n <= 5^(n-1).

For the OPPOSITE cap {x>=0}, the same 3^n sections are proper but
EVERY supporting section is F. Its necessary inequality becomes

  3^n + (5^n-3^n) + 5^(n-1) <= 0,

which is impossible. Thus the opposite cap cannot be minimizing at
both endpoints. This rules out balancing that particular plateau's
horizontal normal merely by adding its opposite. It does not rule
out other tilted normals or a different actual global plateau.

## 4. Facet-free global maxima form an empty exposed lattice polytope

Assume now a convex induced family with d>=2, and assume every
positive fiber has zero (d-1)-measure on every supporting plane.
Let beta>0 be the global maximum mixed depth. Then:

(a) Any attaining cap through one global maximizer STRICTLY
excludes every other distinct global maximizer.

(b) There are at most 2^n maximizing points, with distinct bases.
Their bases are precisely the integer points of their convex hull,
and every such base is an exposed vertex of this hull.

Proof of (a). A positive margin at another maximizer permits
parallel translation to its boundary, removing positive volume
from its own interior fiber and contradicting maximal depth. A
zero margin would give a common minimizing cap with A>0 and no
positive-measure supporting sections, contradicting (1). Thus the
margin must be strictly negative.

For (b), strict interpolation from the cited note excludes two
distinct maximizers with the same parity, including two points in
one fiber, so the set is finite with size at most 2^n. Let an integer
base p be a convex combination of maximizing bases, and form the
same combination y of their full points. Convexity gives y in S;
quasiconcavity and global maximality give depth beta at y. If at
least two distinct points occur with positive coefficients, an
attaining cap through y has strictly negative margins at every
participating point distinct from y, by (a). Its zero margin at y
cannot be their weighted average. Hence every integer combination
is trivial. The hull therefore has no additional integer point,
and no listed base lies in the convex hull of the others.

There is also an explicit exposing functional. Fix a maximizing
point y_i=(p_i,x_i). A minimal positive continuous-normal circuit
of actual active caps exists, by the finite critical-cover argument
already cited. Write these through-point margins as

  a_j.(z-p_i)+u_j.(x-x_i),
  lambda_j>0, sum_j lambda_j u_j=0.

By (a) each margin is negative at every other maximizing point.
Their weighted sum gives

  (sum_j lambda_j a_j).(p_l-p_i)<0   for every l!=i.

Thus sum_j lambda_j a_j exposes p_i among all maximizing bases.
When there is just one base the exposed-vertex conclusion is
trivial. These statements use the facet-free hypothesis and do not
establish an arbitrary-body depth bound. QED.

## 4.1 The exact limit of transferring exterior face flux by coverage

`candidate cdad0ee8b68e978a`
proves that, on each actual positive fiber, a finite closed cap cover
continues to cover after ALL zero-local-volume members are discarded.
Consequently an E-face's delta-weighted measure can be bounded by the
sum of delta-weighted recipient-cap TRACES on that same face. This is
legitimate even for closed boundary faces and d=1.

Those traces cannot simply be replaced by the recipients' own section
measures. The cited exact triangle example has an empty face of length
2 covered by two positive caps whose own section lengths sum to
4epsilon. Three covering normals even admit positive balance. Their
ratio is unbounded. Also the recipient caps in a global cover need
not belong to the particular critical circuit in (4). Thus (4) plus
coverage does not yet give cancellation of the external flux.

## 5. Scope

The new unconditional conclusion is the oriented inequality (1)
and its simultaneous version (4). The later note
`candidate 5cb6b3de949f5208` gives
an exact actual-body counterexample to exclusion of all balanced
supporting-facet configurations at arbitrary global maxima. It has
n=2, any d>=1, and global depth 1/3 at three consecutive integer
bases. In its d=1 form both active caps satisfy A=12 and exterior
empty-face flux 21, and their normals balance. Thus the inequalities
here are compatible with an actual global same-parity plateau.

That depth lies ABOVE OC's gamma_d/4 target. A stronger mechanism
using a genuinely below-target or minimizing-body hypothesis is
not excluded by this counterexample. No OC proof, arbitrary-faceted
global parity theorem, or substitution of single-cap stationarity
for global maximality is made.

The further parameter family in
`candidate 96f963f75f5ed816` has at least 2s+1
global maximizing bases for every integer s>=1, at fixed n=2 and
every fixed d>=1. Thus an arbitrary-faceted finite count bound in
terms of n,d alone is also false. The facet-free subclass statements
in Section 4 remain unaffected.
